title: Daily routine
sub: me levanto, me ducho, me acuesto
can: Describe your day in order, from waking up to going to bed.
doneText: You can now talk through your day in order with reflexive verbs.

skills.stem: Boot verbs: me acuesto, me despierto

discover.intro: The same verbs appear in both colours. Spot what the little word me changes.

groups.label: Without me
lines: I put the children to bed.

discover.question: What does me add in the blue sentences?
options: It shows you do the action to yourself: I get myself up, I shower myself.
It makes the sentence more polite.
It means the action happens in the morning.
discover.nudge: Not quite. In orange, who or what gets lifted, showered or put to bed? And in blue?
discover.reveal: These are reflexive verbs: the action comes back to you. Their dictionary form ends in -se (levantarse), and you put me, te, se, nos, os or se in front of the verb:

hooks.title: Putting a day in order

learn.sub: Tap any row to hear it

blocks.text: Acostarse (to go to bed) and despertarse (to wake up) are boot verbs, like tener and querer. In acostarse the o becomes ue, in despertarse the e becomes ie: me acuesto, me despierto. Nosotros and vosotros keep the plain vowel: nos acostamos, nos despertamos.
Spanish days run late: a light breakfast, lunch at 2 or 3pm, sometimes a siesta, dinner at 9 or 10pm, and bed well after midnight at the weekend.

blocks.title: You already know one
a: My name is {name} (literally: I call myself {name}).
blocks.note: Llamarse is reflexive. Without me, llamar just means to call someone.

blocks.text: With parts of the body Spanish uses el or los, not "my": me lavo los dientes (I brush my teeth), me lavo el pelo (I wash my hair).

phrases.en: What time do you go to bed?

phrases.es: Los fines de semana no madrugo.
phrases.en: I don't get up early at the weekend.

write.title: Say it in your own words
write.task: Describe a normal day on your trip, in order: when you wake up, three things you do, and when you go to bed.
write.starter: Primero me despierto a las…  Luego…  Al final…
write.model: Primero me despierto a las ocho y me ducho. Luego desayuno y salgo a pasear. Por la tarde me echo la siesta. Al final me acuesto a las doce.
checklist: Reflexive verbs have me in front: me levanto, me ducho
Order words: primero, luego, después, al final
Boot verbs: me acuesto, me despierto

boss.title: Sharing a dorm in Barcelona
boss.persona: You are Jordi, a friendly guy from Barcelona sharing a hostel dorm with the learner. You chat about daily routines (what time people get up, shower, eat and go to bed) so you don't disturb each other, and about plans in Barcelona. Speak Spanish, not Catalan. Use tú.

turns.npc: ¡Buenas! Oye, ¿a qué hora te levantas mañana?
turns.en: Hi! Hey, what time are you getting up tomorrow?
choices: Me levanto a las siete.
Te levantas a las siete.
Te levantas is "you get up". About yourself: me levanto.
Levanto a las siete.
Without me it means "I lift" something. Getting up is me levanto.

turns.npc: Vale. ¿Y te duchas por la mañana o por la noche?
turns.en: OK. And do you shower in the morning or at night?
choices: Me ducho por la mañana.
Se ducha por la mañana.
Se ducha is he or she. About yourself: me ducho.
Ducho por la mañana.
Without me, you'd be showering someone else. Me ducho.

turns.npc: ¿Y a qué hora te acuestas normalmente?
turns.en: And what time do you usually go to bed?
choices: Normalmente me acuesto a las once.
Normalmente me acosto a las once.
Acostarse is a boot verb: me acuesto.
Normalmente me acuesta a las once.
Acuesta is he or she. About yourself: me acuesto.

turns.npc: ¡Uf, muy temprano para Barcelona! ¿Cenamos juntos primero, a las diez?
turns.en: Wow, very early for Barcelona! Shall we have dinner together first, at ten?
choices: Vale, primero cenamos y luego nos acostamos.
Vale, primero cenamos y luego nos acuestamos.
Nosotros is outside the boot: nos acostamos.
Vale, primero cenamos y luego me acostamos.
Acostamos is nosotros, so nos: nos acostamos.

boss.closingEn: Perfect! Good night, see you tomorrow.
boss.chatOpening: ¿Y qué vas a hacer mañana en Barcelona?
boss.chatOpeningEn: And what are you going to do tomorrow in Barcelona?
